question: Can an external reader of the byte stored at city +0x58 be proved from the bounded generated indexed-load candidates?

scope.stopCondition: Reproduce the indexed byte-load sites in sub_82D019F0, cross-check their instruction words against the supported image, and stop when no candidate is joined to the producer's city +0x58 pointer and pointer provenance remains ambiguous.
scope.boundary: This is a bounded candidate check of one generated function, not a program-wide reader census. It does not prove absence of other indexed, indirect, computed-address, functionless, or out-of-interval readers.

dependencies.use: Provides the city +0x58 indexed writer and the distinct same-function prior-byte read.
Identifies sub_82D019F0 as a cost-factor helper while leaving its input and pointer provenance unresolved.

staticResult.candidateCensus: Generated code contains 18 lbzx sites in sub_82D019F0. Thirteen use one of the fixed-register operands in r20, r23, or r25; five use the fixed-register operand in r22. The previously reported 21 total and 8/13 split cannot be reproduced from the tracked candidate-selection criteria, which are not recorded.
staticResult.readerBoundary: The 18 raw words decode as lbzx. Generated-code flow forms the candidate addresses using the fixed-register operands above and computed r4 or r11 operands. Function entry also reads city-table halfwords at +0x30 and +0x32, but no candidate load is joined to the separate city +0x58 pointer saved by sub_82D00C78. The computed address ranges and any alias to city +0x58 remain unresolved, so no external reader is proved.

runtimeObservation.qualification: No execution, actual city +0x58 byte value, external reader, or visible effect was observed.

currentEvidence.method: Narrow generated-code census of sub_82D019F0, followed by one foreground read-only raw-word query at radius zero for all 18 guest PCs. Each word decodes to PowerPC lbzx (opcode 31, XO 87).

entries.result: All 18 generated sites are confirmed as lbzx by the corresponding supported-image words.
Fixed-register operands and computed offsets do not establish an alias to the city +0x58 pointer; the reader question stops at ambiguous address provenance.

currentEvidence.qualification: Generated code supplied candidate localization and register flow; exact image words independently confirm the 18 indexed byte-load opcodes. This does not establish any city +0x58 alias or a program-wide absence of readers.

guards: Do not promote the unreproduced 21/8/13 filter or infer its missing selection rule.
Do not identify any of the indexed byte loads as a city +0x58 reader without proving the effective address aliases that pointer.
Do not treat this one-function candidate set as proof that no external reader exists elsewhere.
Do not infer a gameplay effect or runtime behavior from these loads.
conclusion: The bounded generated-code lead reproduces 18 indexed byte loads inside sub_82D019F0, and the supported image confirms all 18 instruction words. Thirteen use fixed-register operands r20, r23, or r25 and five use r22. None is proved to read the city +0x58 byte stored by sub_82D00C78; pointer provenance stops before that alias can be established. The earlier 21/8/13 candidate filter is not recoverable from tracked evidence, and no external reader or visible effect is established.
